mainProgression.progression: I - bVII - IV (Verse) | V - bVII - IV - I (Chorus & Solo)
mainProgression.progressionDescription: Classic rock-influenced grunge harmony: the verse anchors on a gritty A Mixolydian riff (A - G - D), while the chorus and epic outro solo re-center on E major (E - G - D - A).

sectionProgressions.description: Stone Gossard's signature syncopated A5 riff punctuated by D/F# and G double-stops

sectionProgressions.section: Chorus ('Oh I, oh I'm still alive')
sectionProgressions.description: Massive open-chord stadium progression that lifts the tonal gravity up to E major
Tension-building power chord shift before launching back into the final chorus and outro solo
Two-minute Hendrix/Ace Frehley-inspired lead guitar marathon by Mike McCready

harmonicFunction: A (I) - Gritty Mixolydian home base of the main riff
G (bVII) - Borrowed subtonic chord providing classic 70s arena-rock weight
D (IV) - Subdominant chord bridging the G chord back to A or E
E (V / Tonic in Chorus) - Acts as the triumphant harmonic launchpad for the chorus and outro solo

techniques.name: Syncopated Riffing & Pentatonic Wah Soloing
techniques.description: Combining palm-muted open A-string pedal riffs with expressive minor pentatonic string bending, rapid pull-off licks, and wah-pedal filter sweeps

notes: A5 Riff: X-0-7-6-5-X (A major triad on D, G, B strings)
E Minor Pentatonic Box 1 (12th fret) for McCready's solo
sequence: Strike the open A string and slide up into the A major triad (7th fret D, 6th fret G, 5th fret B)
Catch the syncopated G and D double-stops on the 5th and 7th frets
Transition to big, ringing open E, G, D, and A chords in the chorus
For the outro solo, attack the 12th-fret E minor pentatonic box with wide bends and rhythmic wah sweeps
tips: Let the open A string drone slightly beneath the movable triad shapes in the main riff
Keep your picking hand relaxed during the fast repeating pull-off triplets in the solo
Rock the wah pedal in time with your bends to make the high notes scream

sections.name: Intro & Main Riff
sections.description: Stone Gossard's unmistakable opening guitar riff blending an open A pedal with movable triad and double-stop voicings.
notes: Hit the open A string firmly on beat 1
Accent the C# (6th fret G string) and A (7th fret D string)
End the phrase with the F#5 to G5 power chord slide

sections.name: Anthemic Chorus
sections.description: Full, wide-open chords (E - G - D - A) creating the massive 'I'm still alive' chorus hook.
notes: Let all six strings ring out on E and G
Hold each chord for a full bar at 75 BPM
Add subtle sus4 embellishments on the D and A chords

sections.name: Outro Solo Pentatonic Climax
sections.description: Mike McCready's high-octane 12th-position E minor pentatonic solo lick over the E - G - D - A vamp.
notes: Attack the 15th-fret B string and 14th-fret G string with fiery vibrato
Use your index finger at fret 12 as a pivot for the fast pull-offs
Engage a wah pedal for vocal-like filter sweeps

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul Standard (Stone Gossard) & Fender Stratocaster (Mike McCready)
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for Gossard's crunchy rhythm riff; Neck/Bridge single-coil for McCready's solo

effects.distortion: Ibanez TS9 Tube Screamer pushing the Marshall preamp for solos
effects.delay: Subtle studio delay on the outro solo
effects.other: Dunlop Cry Baby Wah (essential for the outro solo climax)

beginner.title: Chorus Chords & Basic Riff Root Notes
steps: Master the four open chords of the chorus: E, G, D, and A
Practice the chorus loop at 75 BPM holding each chord for four beats
Play the simplified power-chord version of the verse riff (A5 - G5 - D5)

intermediate.title: Authentic Gossard Riff & Double-Stops
steps: Fret the movable A major triad at frets 7-6-5 with the open A string pedal
Execute the syncopated G and D double-stops cleanly
Connect the verse, chorus, and B5-F#5-D-E bridge seamlessly

advanced.title: McCready's Two-Minute Outro Solo
steps: Master the 12th-position E minor pentatonic repeating pull-off patterns
Coordinate wah-pedal filter sweeps with full-step bends on the B and high E strings
Build solo intensity across the entire two-minute outro progression

commonMistakes: Rushing the laid-back 75 BPM tempo during the syncopated main riff
Failing to mute the unused strings when sliding into the 7th-fret A triad
Blowing all your solo energy in the first 4 bars instead of pacing the build
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Main verse riff slow accuracy drill at 60 BPM → 75 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus open chord transitions with sus4 embellishments
5 minutes: 12th-fret E minor pentatonic pull-off endurance sequences
5 minutes: Full outro jam over an E - G - D - A backing loop
focusAreas: Syncopated double-stop timing in the main riff
Clean string muting during open A pedal passages
Pentatonic bending pitch accuracy and wah control
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 75 BPM and subdivide in sixteenth notes
Lock the double-stop accents into the off-beats of beats 2 and 3
Practice transitioning from 8th-note phrases to 16th-note sextuplets in the solo
